# secops-statistical-hunter

Agentic skill for Google SecOps SIEM multi-stage statistical outlier hunting.

Key instructions for agents:
1. METHODOLOGY COMMENT HEADER (MANDATORY): Always prepend every generated multi-stage search query with a structured comment block explaining the Hunting Goal, Target Telemetry, Statistical Model, Mathematical Rationale (why this math fits the threat behavior), and Sensitivity Boundary.
2. CONSULTATIVE ROUTING: When users ask open-ended questions about finding outliers (e.g., beaconing, exfiltration, lateral movement), consult the Threat-to-Statistical-Model Decision Matrix in SKILL.md. Recommend a mathematical model (e.g., PERIODIC_BEACON_JITTER with CV < 0.20, or MODIFIED_Z_SCORE_MAD with M_Z > 3.0) and explain physical trade-offs.
3. SEARCH-ONLY EXECUTION (CRITICAL): Multi-stage queries (stage ... { ... }) are strictly Search & Dashboard queries. The Google SecOps Detection Rules engine DOES NOT support multi-stage DAG pipelines or `stage` syntax. NEVER offer or suggest converting a multi-stage search query into a real-time detection alert rule. Only offer ad-hoc execution (udm_search), dashboard widget export, or scheduled hunting searches.
4. BOUNDARY WITH SECOPS-YARA-L: Use secops-yara-l strictly for UDM field name resolution (e.g. principal.asset.ip) and scalar functions. Do NOT adopt rule-building templates from secops-yara-l.
5. SCOPE EXCLUSION GUARDRAIL: Never use UEBA metric functions (metrics.*) or Entity Risk Score (graph.risk_score) in ad-hoc time range queries. Those require fixed batch schedules and belong in secops-risk-analytics. Use raw UDM_EVENTS or RULE_DETECTIONS with inline window.*, math.*, arrays.* functions.
6. BOUNDARY GUIDANCE: Provide semantic tiers (CONSERVATIVE, BALANCED, AGGRESSIVE, NOISE CLIFF). Warn users if a threshold enters the Noise Cliff (e.g. CV > 0.50 or M_Z < 1.5). Offer Pre-Flight 24h decile probes to inspect empirical score distributions.
7. ASYNC LRO WATCHDOG: When executing searches via udm_search or Chronicle API, run asynchronously and watch polling via Jetski's `schedule` tool (e.g., 30s backoff). Never run a synchronous sleep loop. Check progress deltas and quota starvation.
